column3: The web dialog imports plugins/automations/cron.ts (parseCron, nextCron) instead of mirroring it: cronProblem returns the server's own CronError text, or 'never fires', and blocks Create. cronInWords says 'every N' only for steps that divide the hour or the day
column4: Importing keeps the rules exact with no second copy to drift; cron.ts is pure TypeScript with no Worker imports. The step wording matches how nextCron expands */N within a field
column5: web/src/lib/automations.test.ts runs the same bad crons as plugins/automations/cron.test.ts
